bullets: ‘Marley was dead: to begin with.’: blunt, comic, gothic opening; insistence on death sets up the ghost.
‘Oh! But he was a tight-fisted hand at the grindstone, Scrooge!’: exclamations; narrator’s disapproval.
The asyndetic list ‘squeezing, wrenching, grasping, scraping, clutching, covetous, old sinner!’: grasping verbs; religious judgement.
‘Hard and sharp as flint, from which no steel had ever struck out generous fire’: no warmth has ever come from him; fire = generosity.
‘secret, and self-contained, and solitary as an oyster’: polysyndeton and sibilance; isolation.
‘The cold within him froze his old features’: inner cold.
Nobody stops him in the street; even blind men’s dogs avoid him: total isolation, comic exaggeration.
core.p: The narrator establishes Marley’s death and describes Scrooge.

bullets: Fred ‘all in a glow’ vs Scrooge’s coldness: **juxtaposition**.

Scrooge: ‘every idiot who goes about with “Merry Christmas” on his lips, should be boiled with his own pudding, and buried with a stake of holly through his heart’: comic hyperbole; violent rejection of Christmas.
Collectors: ‘Many thousands are in want of common necessaries’.
Scrooge: ‘Are there no prisons?’ ‘decrease the surplus population’; ‘It’s not my business’.
core.h: Extract 2: Fred and the charity collectors
core.p: Fred’s cheerful invitation and the collectors’ request.

bullets: Gothic build-up: the knocker, bells, cellar noises, the chain dragging upstairs.
Scrooge’s scepticism and joke: ‘more of gravy than of grave’.
Marley’s wail and the removal of his jaw bandage: horror.
‘I wear the chain I forged in life’; ‘Mankind was my business’.
The phantoms outside: ‘The misery with them all was, clearly, that they sought to interfere, for good, in human matters, and had lost the power for ever.’
core.p: Marley appears in chains and warns Scrooge.

model: Rhetorical questions about prisons and workhouses
exam.q: Explore how Dickens presents Scrooge’s attitude to others in this extract (Stave 1, the charity collectors). (20 marks)
exam.tip: Notice the word ‘business’: it returns in Marley’s speech.

mistakes.r: Analyse the specific words and their effect.

quotes.q: buried with a stake of holly through his heart

quotes.a: Denial of responsibility; answered by Marley’s ‘Mankind was my business’.

quotes.q: had lost the power for ever

summary: Stave 1 contains the most likely part (a) extracts: the opening portrait of Scrooge, the visits of Fred and the charity collectors, and Marley’s Ghost; learn what to say about each.

terms.d: Opening that establishes character and situation.
